status: Proposal; not an approved implementation story

prdGap: The checked-out PRD mandates source review and immutable confirmation but does not explicitly mandate editable source or code downloads. Those are a user-requested product extension, not an already implemented PRD obligation.

functional.description: Allow an authorized author to edit Studio source from the Code tab without mutating any existing confirmed revision.
functional.rationale: Support expert corrections while retaining the checklist-first workflow and immutable trust boundary.
acceptance: Given readable source and edit permission, entering Edit creates a distinct working draft while the base immutable revision remains unchanged.
Code changes remain identifiable as unconfirmed until validated and explicitly confirmed.
Code draft changes participate in page Save, dirty-state and navigation protection; tab switching and background reads preserve the working buffer.

Combined page Save commits authoring first, then compatible code using returned freshness; a failed or incompatible second save preserves local code, reports partial state and blocks validation/execution until resolved.

functional.description: Offer an authorized source download from the Code tab with explicit revision identity, content and portability meaning.
functional.rationale: Users need to obtain the code they are reviewing; a Studio artifact must not be mislabeled as a runnable standalone Playwright file.
acceptance: Given a retained source revision, downloading produces that selected revision's exact source artifact with server-provided identity and hash.
Downloaded artifacts contain reference identifiers rather than resolved secrets.
The interface distinguishes Studio source download from a standalone Playwright export; unsupported portability is not promised.

functional.description: Submit manually edited code through authoritative server validation and review before it can become a runnable confirmed revision.
functional.rationale: The existing validator and confirmation contract protect generated and manual source equally.
acceptance: Manual preparation validates schema, bounded step AST, declared references and current policy without invoking AI to replace the user's source.
Rejected source shows bounded per-step diagnostics and creates no runnable confirmed revision.
Successful preparation creates a new immutable candidate requiring the exact revision/hash and freshness inputs to be confirmed.
Generated and manual preparations both reach awaiting-confirmation; preparation must not stamp confirmation identity/time or make the candidate READY before the author confirms it.

functional.description: Keep every editable code step associated with its checklist identity and original text, and make any divergence visible.
functional.rationale: Step-level progress and evidence depend on ordered source-step mapping; code edits cannot assert that English and behavior are automatically equivalent.
acceptance: Manual edits preserve the current artifact's valid ordered step mapping.
Review renders actual validated code/actions and identifies user-edited provenance instead of claiming unchanged AI translation.
Checklist edits cannot silently regenerate or overwrite manual source; the user must select an explicit preparation path.

functional.description: Preserve immutable source version history and provenance so each run identifies the exact confirmed version accepted for execution.
functional.rationale: Execution needs one authoritative version, independent of later draft/code edits.
acceptance: New generated or manually edited source creates a new immutable revision rather than editing an old revision in place.
Manual revision provenance identifies its base revision and author, without fabricating AI provenance for edited source.
An accepted execution continues using its snapshotted revision after a later authoring change.
Equal artifact hashes from distinct successful preparation/authorship events retain distinct revision identities; a retry of the same captured attempt returns the same outcome.

functional.description: Reject stale code saves, validations, confirmations and executions instead of silently accepting outdated source.
functional.rationale: Code introduces an additional execution-affecting input into the existing optimistic concurrency contract.
acceptance: An edit to source or configuration invalidates runnable readiness for the current draft.
Concurrent authoring returns a conflict and preserves the losing client's local edits for recovery.
A delayed generated/manual preparation result cannot publish against inputs that have moved.
The API refuses execution when confirmation does not match all current execution-affecting inputs.

Execute identifies the revision/hash and current freshness values the client intends to run; the API accepts only that exact current confirmed revision, never a newer different confirmation selected in a race.
An unchanged compatible confirmed revision remains runnable after an optional preparation failure; compileStatus alone is neither a readiness grant nor a readiness revocation.

Existing authoring/Steps/context/config writers compare complete caller expected freshness with saved state; all preparation success/failure/deadline/cancellation/abandonment settlements recheck captured request identity and freshness, so older work cannot clear a newer manual candidate/request or revoke unchanged confirmed readiness.

functional.description: Show distinct working, validated candidate and confirmed source states so the user can tell what would run and what was downloaded.
functional.rationale: Editable source would otherwise make the Code tab's current saved-source guarantee misleading.
acceptance: The visible source carries a human-readable state and immutable revision identity when one exists.
Unsaved local edits never appear as confirmed source.
Save, preparation, review/confirmation, download and Run states remain understandable during loading, empty and error states.
The selected last-run source remains inspectable under that execution snapshot identity after later draft or confirmation changes.

functional.description: Preserve CSI ownership, current secret-reference policy and runtime compatibility checks across code editing, downloading and execution.
functional.rationale: Code editing and downloads expose existing protected resources; they do not bypass ordinary authorization or broaden execution capability.
acceptance: Unauthorized callers cannot read/download source or create/confirm manual revisions.
Manual code cannot access an undeclared or unauthorized variable/secret reference.
Historical source remains preserved when runtime policy revocation blocks running it.

nonFunctional.description: Manual source remains subject to the same bounded allowlist validator and operation-only execution boundary as generated source.
nonFunctional.metric: All existing forbidden-node/method fixtures remain rejected; no browser-evaluate, filesystem, process, arbitrary import or unrestricted JavaScript path is introduced.

nonFunctional.description: Revision and accepted-execution identity remains durable and consistent under concurrent edits and retries.
nonFunctional.metric: Race tests produce one conditional winner; losing saves/confirmations/preparations cannot replace current source; accepted executions retain their immutable revision.

nonFunctional.description: Source editing and download actions support keyboard use and explicit understandable saved/candidate/confirmed/error states.
nonFunctional.metric: Keyboard-only author can enter edit, change source, save, inspect diagnostics, confirm and download; focused errors associate with the relevant step.

constraints.description: Keep the existing bounded Playwright step language and trusted typed-operation executor unless a separately approved architecture changes that boundary.
constraints.impact: Editing exposes supported per-step source, not arbitrary TypeScript projects. The proposed editor must explicitly supersede ADR-002 §30 for working/candidate views while preserving the confirmed-view identity guarantee.

constraints.description: Maintain checklist-first no-code authoring and exact revision review/confirmation before execution; no runtime AI or silent regeneration.
constraints.impact: Manual source is an optional expert path requiring clear mode transitions and reconfirmation.

constraints.description: Use existing React/TypeScript/MUI, centralized API client, MSW contracts and backend/runner bounded contexts.
constraints.impact: No editor library, Git service or new runtime dependency is preselected without verified need.

constraints.description: This pipeline delivers analysis and a reviewable proposal only, without production implementation or rewriting the existing PRD/architecture.
constraints.impact: Decisions and future file changes are proposals; no acceptance status implies feature delivery.

constraints.description: Python export is retired; standalone Playwright export, code import, Git synchronization and revision rollback are not established requirements in the checked-out PRD.
constraints.impact: Do not bundle these capabilities into the recommended first slice without explicit scope decisions.

assumptions.description: The requested edit capability means changing bounded code that Studio executes, rather than executing arbitrary uploaded Playwright projects.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: An unrestricted-code product needs a separate isolation, policy and runtime architecture.

assumptions.description: A faithful revision-identified Studio source download satisfies the immediate download need; standalone local execution is a distinct optional follow-up.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A portable package requires a verified adapter/runtime contract rather than merely wrapping snippets.

assumptions.description: Existing CSI-scoped author permissions can govern code editing without introducing a new product role in this first slice.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Authorization policy must distinguish code authors from ordinary checklist authors.

proposedDecisions.description: Native immutable Studio revisions remain execution authority; edit a separate bounded manual draft. Git integration and full TypeScript execution remain separate scope.

Keep existing checklist/context counters and add codeDraftRevision, GENERATED/MANUAL authoringMode and server codeDraftHash; enforce full freshness tuple at every writer and acceptance boundary. This includes existing authoring writers and all background outcomes, using immutable captured identity for workers rather than client-body expectations.

Generated and manual preparation create unconfirmed immutable candidates; only explicit exact-revision approval makes new source runnable. Reconcile current auto-accept publication and legacy current eligibility during rollout.

Save append-only manual authoring checkpoints, including invalid bounded syntax, and retain them across deliberate regeneration. Reuse captured preparation attempts for manual validation; deduplicate retries by event identity.
Download a selected persisted validated revision as a ZIP with exact canonical source.artifact.json plus allowlisted manifest.json. No unsaved-draft or standalone executable export in first slice.

domainModel.description: Mutable authoring inputs, configuration and freshness counters belonging to one immutable registered CSI.
Server-validated immutable artifact with canonical hash, source/configuration context, provenance and write-once confirmation metadata.
relationships: may reference parent revision for manual edits

domainModel.description: Durable accepted attempt that snapshots a confirmed revision, CSI, environment and current runtime provenance.

interactions.description: Author enters Code, creates a working draft from an identified source, changes supported step code, saves, validates, reviews and confirms the new revision.
Author selects a readable source revision and downloads its exact Studio artifact with revision identity and explicit portability semantics.

edgeCases.scenario: Two authors edit the same source version
edgeCases.handling: Conditional persistence rejects the stale save and keeps its local text available to reconcile.

edgeCases.scenario: Checklist or referenced nonsecret values change while manual source exists
edgeCases.handling: Invalidate readiness and explain that manual source needs explicit revalidation or intentional replacement; do not silently regenerate.

edgeCases.scenario: Manual source uses unsupported TypeScript or an unauthorized reference
edgeCases.handling: Reject before any runnable candidate/confirmation, using bounded diagnostics.

edgeCases.scenario: User downloads while local source differs from selected saved revision
edgeCases.handling: Clearly identify the saved revision being downloaded; do not imply local edits were confirmed or exported.

edgeCases.scenario: User has no confirmed or validated source yet
edgeCases.handling: Show a preparation path and an honest source-unavailable state.

edgeCases.scenario: Policy or runtime upgrade makes an old confirmed revision incompatible
edgeCases.handling: Preserve historical source, reject incompatible execution and require explicit validation/confirmation against current policy.

terminology.definition: An ordered JSON artifact of supported per-step Playwright expressions; not a standalone Playwright test file.
Mutable manually edited source that has not yet been validated and confirmed.
One persisted validated artifact/context identity; later edits create a new revision.
The exact revision and artifact hash the author accepted, runnable only while all freshness and current policy checks still match.
The artifact format version; distinct from source revision identity, mutable draft counters and execution snapshot revisions.
Faithful retrieval of an identified Studio artifact; portable Playwright export would be a separately labeled derived format.

openQuestions.question: Does the desired download need a Studio artifact for inspection/archival, or a standalone locally runnable Playwright package? Recommended first slice is exact Studio source download.
Should the existing CSI author permission govern manual source edits, or must code editing require a dedicated elevated permission?
What revision/code retention and maximum editable-source limits are required beyond existing artifact caps?
